ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciproc.summary: Neither library has complex multiplication. Mathlib supplies the ambient field theory a CM development would sit on — `NumberField.IsCMField` with the maximal real subfield and complex conjugation, the idele group and idele class group, class groups and Dedekind-domain ideal theory, `WeierstrassCurve.j` with `exists_variableChange_of_j_eq`, and integral models/good-and-bad reduction; Tau Ceti supplies ideal-theoretic ray class groups with a modulus, the Artin symbol at unramified primes with Chebotarev, and a substantial elliptic-curve isogeny theory (the Hom group, degree multiplicativity, kernels, separability, Frobenius factorisation). Genuinely missing is everything the roadmap names: CM types and reflex norms, orders of a number field other than the maximal one (so no proper invertible ideals, no conductor, no ring class group), the analytic uniformization ℓattice → elliptic curve, the main theorem of complex multiplication, class polynomials, ring and ray class *fields* as fields, algebraic Hecke characters, Tate modules, abelian varieties and the Shimura–Taniyama formula. The roadmap's own targets are therefore almost entirely unbuilt; its CM.2 is by construction a re-export of ShimuraVarieties:V5, which is itself unbuilt.

targets.target: Orders in CM fields (subrings of finite index in the ring of integers) and their conductors
targets.note: Mathlib defines a CM field (totally complex quadratic over its maximal totally real subfield) and its complex conjugation, but has no notion of an order: only the maximal order `𝓞 K` exists. `grep -rn 'an order in|non-maximal order|order of conductor'` over both libraries returns nothing in this sense, and the only `conductor` declarations are `DirichletCharacter.conductor` and a `Subalgebra`-conductor lemma for quadratic splitting.

targets.target: Proper invertible ideals of an order and the ideal class group of an order, distinguished from the class group of the maximal order
targets.note: Mathlib's `ClassGroup R` is the Picard group of fractional ideals of a Dedekind domain, so it is only the class group of the *maximal* order; Tau Ceti's ray class groups are quotients of ideals prime to a modulus inside `𝓞 K`. Proper (= with multiplier ring exactly the order) invertible ideals of a non-maximal order, and their class group, exist nowhere.

targets.target: CM types Φ ⊂ Hom(K,ℂ) with Φ ⊔ Φ̄ = Hom(K,ℂ), and non-Galois CM types
targets.note: The two ingredients (complex embeddings and their conjugation, complex conjugation on a CM field) are in Mathlib, but no set-of-embeddings structure with the CM-type condition is defined; `grep -rn -i 'CM type'` over both libraries returns nothing.

targets.target: The reflex field and reflex norm of a CM type, on the existing torus/idele objects
targets.note: The idele group and idele class group of a number field are in Mathlib, and the field norm is there, but no reflex field and no reflex norm N_Φ is defined in either library. `grep -rn -i 'reflex'` returns nothing.

targets.target: Conjugation and change-of-type formulas for CM types
targets.note: Depends on the CM-type definition, which does not exist.

duplicates.note: V5 explicitly says 'Construct CM types, reflex types, reflex norms, and the Tate-module action', which is the whole of CM.0 in greater generality.
M0 constructs the field of definition of the determinant condition and identifies it with the reflex field, overlapping CM.0's reflex-field target.
D3 defines the conjugacy class {µ}, its Galois action and the reflex field as the fixed field of its stabiliser — the reflex field of CM.0 is the special case of a CM torus.

targets.target: The elliptic curve ℂ/𝔞 attached to a complex lattice / ideal of an order, with its order action
targets.note: Elliptic curves exist only as Weierstrass equations; there is no Weierstrass ℘-function, no Eisenstein series g₂/g₃ of a lattice, and no uniformization ℂ/Λ ≅ E(ℂ). Tau Ceti's `ComplexTorus` is the algebraic torus (ℂˣ)ⁿ of toric geometry, not ℂ/Λ.

targets.target: Identification of isomorphism classes of such curves with proper ideal classes of the order
targets.note: Mathlib proves that equal j-invariants give isomorphic curves over an algebraically closed field, which is the classification input; the bijection with proper ideal classes needs both the lattice construction and the order class group, neither of which exists.

targets.target: Automorphism factors at j = 0 and j = 1728 (extra automorphisms of the curve)
targets.note: Tau Ceti computes the automorphism group of a Weierstrass curve as a group of variable changes, with the j = 0 and j = 1728 characterisations available; this is the only target of this layer with library support, and it is stated for Weierstrass models rather than for lattices.

targets.target: Action of an invertible prime ideal on the curve and its isogeny degree
targets.note: Tau Ceti has a genuine isogeny theory — `Hom(W₁,W₂)` as an additive group, multiplicative degree, kernels, separability and Frobenius factorisation — so the target of an ideal action (an isogeny of prescribed degree) has a home. The action of an ideal itself is absent, since it needs the order and the lattice model.

targets.target: Comparison of analytic and algebraic endomorphism rings
targets.note: The algebraic side (End as a ring with no zero divisors, degree multiplicative) is built in Tau Ceti; the analytic side (End(ℂ/Λ) = {α : αΛ ⊆ Λ}) does not exist, so the comparison cannot even be stated. No theorem identifying End with an order in an imaginary quadratic field is present.

duplicates.note: HE.1 constructs CM elliptic curves and cyclic-isogeny pairs over ℂ and descends them to ring class fields — the same complex CM curves and ideal actions as CM.1, used for Heegner points.
A5 proves the Riemann bilinear relations and algebraicity of polarized complex tori, the general form of the analytic-quotient-equals-algebraic-curve comparison CM.1 asks for in dimension one.

targets.target: The main theorem of complex multiplication (the reciprocity law for the Galois action on a CM abelian variety and its torsion)
targets.note: Nothing towards this exists: there are no abelian varieties, no Tate modules (`grep -i tateModule` is empty), and no CM types in either library. The layer is itself framed as importing ShimuraVarieties:V5, which is unbuilt.

targets.target: Ideal, idele and torsion-level dictionaries with a fixed Artin convention
targets.note: Tau Ceti fixes the arithmetic Artin convention at unramified primes (conjugacy-class valued, with functoriality in towers) and has ideal-theoretic ray class groups; Mathlib has the idele class group. The ideal ↔ idele comparison itself — the global reciprocity map — is not proved in either library; Tau Ceti's `ClassFieldTheory/Formation` is the abstract class-formation machinery only, with no arithmetic instance.

targets.target: Separation of base field, CM endomorphism field and reflex field
targets.note: All three notions presuppose CM types and reflex norms, which are absent.

targets.target: Action on torsion and polarizations in a dimension-two example
targets.note: No abelian surfaces, polarizations or torsion-level structures exist in either library.

duplicates.note: V5 states 'Prove the main theorem of complex multiplication' including the Shimura–Taniyama Frobenius calculation and the passage to the full reciprocity law; CM.2 is by its own text a re-import and comparison of exactly that theorem.
V7 handles conjugation and descent for general Shimura data, which subsumes CM.2's Artin-convention bookkeeping for the CM case.

targets.target: The class polynomial H_D(X) = ∏_{[𝔞]} (X − j(𝔞)) over proper ideal classes
targets.note: The j-invariant of a Weierstrass curve exists, but the modular function j on the upper half plane does not (no `jFunction`, no Klein invariant; Mathlib's `UpperHalfPlane.J` is the symplectic matrix, not the modular function), so j(𝔞) for a lattice cannot be written and the product over ideal classes does not exist.

targets.target: Algebraic integrality of the j-values (H_D ∈ ℤ[X])
targets.note: Only the general integral-closure machinery is available; the integrality of singular moduli is not proved.

targets.target: Galois equivariance of the j-values and the identification of the ring class field of an order in an imaginary quadratic field
targets.note: No class field of any kind is constructed in either library: `grep -rn -i 'hilbert class field|ring class field|ray class field'` finds only a passing remark in a Tau Ceti docstring. Tau Ceti's ray class *groups* exist but no abelian extension is attached to them.

targets.target: Ray-class variants using level (modular) functions with admissibility conditions
targets.note: The ray subgroup of a modulus is defined in Tau Ceti; the Weber functions / level functions generating ray class fields are absent.

duplicates.note: HE.1 also proves descent of CM points to ring class fields, so the ring-class-field identification is stated twice.

targets.target: Algebraic Hecke characters attached to CM abelian varieties
targets.note: There is no Hecke character, Größencharakter or idele-class character anywhere: the only `Hecke` declarations in either library are the abstract Hecke ring and its GL₂ instances (Mathlib/NumberTheory/HeckeRing, TauCeti/NumberTheory/HeckeRing), which are double-coset algebras, not characters.

targets.target: Infinity type and finite conductor of such a character
targets.note: Only the conductor of a Dirichlet character (a character of (ℤ/n)ˣ) exists; there is no conductor of an idele class character and no infinity type.

targets.target: Frobenius identities ψ(𝔭) = a_𝔭 at good primes
targets.note: The Artin symbol and its Chebotarev equidistribution are available in Tau Ceti, but there is no L-series of an elliptic curve with proved Euler factors at good primes to match against; Mathlib's `EllipticCurve/LFunction.lean` is not a proved Euler product over the CM decomposition.

targets.target: Comparison of the one-dimensional components of the ℓ-adic representation with the Tate module; splitting of the rank-two representation for a CM curve
targets.note: No Tate module of an elliptic curve or abelian variety is defined in either library (`grep -i tateModule` is empty), so neither the rank-two representation nor its CM decomposition can be stated.

duplicates.note: V5's 'Tate-module action' for CM abelian varieties is the same object CM.4 compares its characters against.
L3 covers totally real abelian and CM constructions, which build on the same CM Hecke characters.

targets.target: The Shimura–Taniyama formula for the reduction of a CM abelian variety
targets.note: Absent; it presupposes CM types and reduction of abelian varieties, neither of which exists.

targets.target: Isogeny graphs of CM elliptic curves at a good prime; ordinary versus supersingular reduction
targets.note: Good/multiplicative/additive reduction classes and integral models are in Mathlib, and Tau Ceti has isogenies with degrees, kernels and the relative Frobenius; but there is no `IsSupersingular`/`IsOrdinary` predicate anywhere (`grep -i supersingular` is empty), so the dichotomy the acceptance clause turns on is not even expressible.

targets.target: Certified complex or CRT computation of class polynomials with proved height/precision bounds
targets.note: Class polynomials do not exist, and no certified-numerics framework for algebraic numbers with error certificates is present in either library.

targets.target: Endomorphism-ring verification as a separate certificate
targets.note: The endomorphism carrier exists in Tau Ceti but is not identified with an order in a quadratic field, and there is no algorithm or certificate for computing it.

duplicates.note: V5 lists 'reduction of CM abelian varieties at suitable primes, the Shimura–Taniyama Frobenius calculation' among its proof obligations, the same statement CM.5 instantiates.

targets.target: Export of ring/ray class fields, torsion fields, Hecke characters and ideal-action theorems to downstream applications
targets.note: This is an interface/re-export task over CM.0–CM.5, none of whose objects exist; it states no new mathematics of its own.

targets.target: Documentation of which level functions generate the asserted field
targets.note: Bookkeeping over the (absent) ray class field construction of CM.3.

targets.target: A worked elliptic ring-class example and a higher-dimensional reflex-field example
targets.note: Acceptance examples for the preceding layers; no independent target.

duplicates.note: The named consumer of CM.6's ring-class-field export already states the same descent to ring class fields as one of its own obligations.
